subject: Re: Using densities from global detection functions in other

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Using densities from global detection functions in other
parts:
Jared:

Many of your suspicions are correct. Fitting a detection function means you are
trying to fit a function to a set of detections; to do a reasonable job of that,
you ought to have ~70 data points to fit that function. That is why you are
seeing complaints by DISTANCE when you attempt to produce detection functions
for your stations (which I presume are points).

When you use the global detection function to derive your point-specific density
estimates, you do indeed have non-independence issues because estimates for all
of your points share the common detection function and hence are correlated.

So there is no free lunch really, if you wish to make comparisons of density
between points, have sufficient data at each point to make the comparisons
legitimate.

Quoting jared zimmerman <jaredaz...@gmail.com>:

> > Dear All,
> >
> > I'm doing a study of habitat associations of songbirds using point transect
> > counts. I would like to generate densities of neotropical migratory birds at
> > the stratum level (by count station, 3 -6 visits per station). For some
> > reason, DISTANCE allows me to generate densities only by using a global
> > detection function. It shows numerous unknown error messages and doesnt
> > complete the analysis when I select detection function to be calculated by
> > stratum alone. It may be a sample size issue. In any case, my question has
> > to do with using densities calculated with a global detection function to
> > run additional (non-DISTANCE) analyses at the stratum level (densities at
> > each count station). I want to see if and how densities at each count
> > station differ with respect to two principal components of my habitat
> > variables. Are there non-independence issues in using densities created from
> > a detection function of *all count stations* in an analyses that tests for
> > differences in densities *between count stations*? Does this weaken the
> > analysis? Is there a better way to proceed? Thank You.
> >
> >
> > Jared Zimmerman
